pr_title: Make proxy Transport return metav1.Status error
pr_body:
Fixed #98479

/sig api-machinery
/assign @p0lyn0mial @sttts

The problem described in #98479 is that when the kube-apiserver proxy is used to access a Service that's not listening, the kube-apiserver apart from correctly returning the error to the client, it also logs an error complaining that "apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status".

The flow of the error log is like the following:
The [err](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fa704c6a883d369d1a4cf273f8dd13516e4a58c/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy/transport.go#L104) returned by the proxy.Transport is then returned to the client via the [responder](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fa704c6a883d369d1a4cf273f8dd13516e4a58c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/rest.go#L203), but when the `responder.scope.err()` calls [ErrorToAPIStatus](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fa704c6a883d369d1a4cf273f8dd13516e4a58c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/responsewriters/writers.go#L284) to interpret the error, it [leaves an error message](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fa704c6a883d369d1a4cf273f8dd13516e4a58c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/responsewriters/status.go#L71) in the apiserver log because the `err` does not implement the [statusError](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5fa704c6a883d369d1a4cf273f8dd13516e4a58c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/responsewriters/status.go#L30) interface.

This PR makes the proxy.Transport return a NewServiceUnavailable error instead.

I manually verified that with this PR, there is no more error message in the apiserver log, though I can't find a simple way to unit test the behavior.

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: apiserver logs error message when using /proxy to an unavailable endpoint
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I upgraded from 1.15 and am using prometheus to scrape my pods via the proxy functionality. Previously no error message was being printed, now with 1.19.9 every try results in an error:

Example url: https://x.x.x.x:6443/api/v1/namespaces/staging/pods/proxy-app-588d688877-6sxfx:80/proxy/metrics

```
E0127 13:45:58.408564       1 status.go:71] apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status: &fmt.wrapError{msg:"error trying to reach service: dial tcp 10.253.41.141:80: connect: connection refused", err:(*net.OpError)(0xc00b58b0e0)}
E0127 13:45:58.746819       1 status.go:71] apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status: &fmt.wrapError{msg:"error trying to reach service: dial tcp 10.253.45.165:80: connect: connection refused", err:(*net.OpError)(0xc005ed2af0)}
E0127 13:45:58.749579       1 status.go:71] apiserver received an error that is not an metav1.Status: &fmt.wrapError{msg:"error trying to reach service: dial tcp 10.253.47.145:80: connect: connection refused", err:(*net.OpError)(0xc00cbd2410)}
```

**What you expected to happen**:

No error message to be logged, since the apiserver anyways returns a corresponding http error code. The least thing I would expect it not to log as an error, but as a debug or info log, since it doesn't actually represent an error.

It returns something like that:

```
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {

  },
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "error trying to reach service: dial tcp 10.253.41.138:80: connect: connection refused",
  "code": 500
}
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Call the proxy functionality on an endpoint that does not listen and will refuse the connection.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

There is a lot of other issues with a similar error message, but I believe they are not interconnected since this has explicitly todo with an error raised from the proxy functionality.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.9
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: on premise
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOs 7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.4.60

review_comments:
Would it be possible to extend `NewServiceUnavailable` so that it could be used with `errors.Is` and `errors.As` method?

I have opened[ a PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92291) that adds a retry mechanism to the `aggregator`. The idea was to intercept errors returned from the round trippers and interpret them. Here is an example - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92291/files?file-filters%5B%5D=.go#diff-ffaa928dbabab1da2e82594be1620b945b37f7fc7256ec1c067abb9af412c4a3R196

Does it make sense ?

Got it.  We can extend the [StatusError](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/838bb6a56760a2abf03bbd42ab3e3a53ed58df13/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors/errors.go#L35),
   * adding a new field to record the original error
   * adding helper functions to create StatusError with original error.
   * adding a Unwrap() method

StatusError is used in many places, we should change its interface with caution. We can begin with making a local extension in k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy, and merge it back when it's mature.

Is this PR breaking existing code though? The PR you linked is still open. It would be hard to justify the complexity of the extension if we don't have a real use case.

I think that we should follow the standard golang way and add an Unwrap() method.

> Is this PR breaking existing code though? The PR you linked is still open. It would be hard to justify the complexity of the extension if we don't have a real use case.

You are right, this PR won't break existing code it will be just a little harder in the future. I'm okay with merging.
